summaries.field: econometrics / model selection and forecast evaluation
summaries.information_need: A researcher wants to understand the model confidence set procedure, which narrows a large collection of competing models or forecasts down to a smaller subset guaranteed to contain the best model with a given level of confidence, adapting automatically to how informative the data are about which model is best.

A researcher wants the formal MCS algorithm that repeatedly applies an equivalence test and an elimination rule to a set of competing objects until no further object is judged significantly inferior, together with the theorem establishing that the resulting surviving set contains the true set of superior objects with the target coverage probability.

A researcher wants the notion of coherency between test and elimination rule, a condition ensuring that a finite-sample version of the model confidence set coverage guarantee holds, together with the reasoning for why coherency can require sacrificing the most powerful equivalence test in favour of one whose rejections point to a specific inferior object.

A researcher wants the definition of MCS p-values, computed from the sequence of p-values generated as models are eliminated one at a time, together with the theorem showing that an object belongs to the model confidence set at a given level exactly when its MCS p-value exceeds that level, illustrated through a worked numerical example.
summaries.answer_type: definition with theorem and worked example

summaries.information_need: A researcher wants the bootstrap equivalence test statistics used to implement the model confidence set procedure in practice, including a quadratic-form test and two multiple t-statistic based tests together with their matching elimination rules, and the theorem describing the asymptotic distribution of these statistics under the null and alternative hypotheses.

A researcher wants to know how the model confidence set is constructed for regression models using the Kullback-Leibler information criterion and related likelihood-based measures such as the AIC and BIC, adjusted with a bootstrap estimate of the effective degrees of freedom, together with the complications that arise when some of the competing regression models are nested.

A researcher wants to understand how intersection-union testing links the model confidence set to the trace-test procedure for selecting cointegration rank, and how the model confidence set relates more broadly to the multiple-comparisons-with-control literature, contrasting its advantages over tests for superior predictive ability that require a pre-specified benchmark model.

A researcher wants to understand how parameter estimation uncertainty complicates the model confidence set when nested forecasting models rely on estimated parameters, along with the resulting need for modified test procedures, together with a discussion contrasting the frequentist model confidence set with an analogous Bayesian approach to model selection based on posterior model probabilities.
summaries.answer_type: discussion of estimation issues and Bayesian contrast

summaries.information_need: A researcher wants Monte Carlo evidence on the size and power properties of the bootstrap model confidence set procedure, measured by how often the true best models are retained and how many models remain in the set, across designs that vary the correlation between alternatives, the degree of separation among their true performances, and the presence of heteroskedastic errors.

A researcher wants Monte Carlo evidence on nested regression model selection performance for the Kullback-Leibler, AIC, and BIC based model confidence sets, comparing how well each criterion isolates the parsimonious true model as the sample size and the correlation among regressors increase.

An analyst wants an inflation forecast comparison across Phillips curve, autoregressive, no-change, and factor-based forecasting models using the model confidence set, applied separately to an earlier volatile subsample and a later calmer subsample, to see which forecasts survive and how the choice of no-change benchmark reconciles conflicting findings in the prior literature.

An analyst wants a Taylor rule regression selection exercise that applies the model confidence set with likelihood-based criteria to a set of interest-rate rule specifications, to determine which combinations of lagged inflation, real activity measures, and interest-rate smoothing best fit the historical policy rate, and how much uncertainty remains about the best specification.
